newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria boosts Biochim by $22 mln state bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria boosts Biochim by $22 mln state bonds.

text.p: Bulgaria's government decided on Thursday to boost the state-owned Biochim assets by $22 million of bad loan bonds and government bonds, issued under a state deposit quarantee law, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said.
"The Finance ministry will sell to the Biochim bad debt loan bonds and bonds issued under a deposit guarantee law to boost its assets by $22 million," told repoters.
The preliminary estimations of Biochim capital gap of $15 million were changed to $22 million because of new provisioning requirements of banks risk assets.
The current operation is aimed at boosting Biochim negative capital to risk assets ratio to zero and is part of attempts to find a foreign partner to take a stake in the bank, Radev said.
Under the scheme, approved by the government, state papers will be purchased by Biochim at a symbolic price of one cent against one dollar par value, Radev said.
The scheme might propose a bigger amount of government paper issued for a state deposit guarantee because of their higher yield and shorter maturity, a finance ministry official said.
Bonds issued under a deposit quarantee law were issued last year with a three year period of maturity and bear a semi-annual interest of LIBOR plus two percentage points.
The bad debt loan bonds were issued in 1994 with a 25 year maturity and bear a semi-annual LIBOR.

Last week the Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in commercial banks and holds some 98 percent in Biochim, sent letters to 25 potential strategic investors offering negotiations on a privatisation deal for the bank.
So far the state had bought some $20 million of bad loan bonds from Biochim at par value of $100.
Under banking standards prescribed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Bulgarian commercial banks are to have six percent capital to risk assets ratio by end-1997.

Under pledges to the IMF, Bulgaria should seal privatisation deals or management contracts for two of its operating state-owned banks by end- September. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
